records.description: Schulich Leader Scholarships are awarded to graduating high school students entering one of 20 partner universities to study science, technology, engineering or mathematics, or to study science, technology, engineering or mathematics as a minor. Half of the 100 annual scholarships are valued at $120,000 for engineering and half at $100,000 for science and mathematics. The programme is funded by the Schulich Foundation and co-administered by UJA Federation of Greater Toronto, and Schulich Leaders can devote their full time and attention to their studies because all of their financial needs are covered over the course of their bachelor degree.

eligibility: Graduating high school students (Student Leader Nominees) entering one of the 20 partner universities
Student entrepreneurs with the drive to launch their own ventures may also apply
Students who qualify must demonstrate academic excellence, leadership, charitableness and financial need
STUDENT LEADERS: applicants must be nominated by their high school
Student Place Holders who apply after their graduating year must be enrolled at one of the 20 partner universities
benefits: $120,000 each for engineering scholarships and $100,000 each for science and mathematics scholarships
100 awards each year across 20 partner universities
All of the recipient's financial needs are covered over the course of their bachelor degree
selection_criteria: Two letters of recommendation, an essay and a transcript are required as part of the nominee's application
official.application_process: Every high school in Canada may submit one graduating student per year for the Schulich Leader Nominee Award (nominations open in September). High schools submit their nominee between 11 January and 27 January 2027; the nominee then submits the scholarship application by 17 February 2027. Universities make offers to the strongest applicants between 8 March and 15 June 2027. Applications outside the nomination window are handled as Student Place Holder applications.
key_dates: High school submits nominee: by 27 January 2027
Nominee submits scholarship application: by 17 February 2027
Universities make offers: 8 March to 15 June 2027

applicant_utility.description: Schulich is a nomination-based award, so the first thing to secure is a high school willing to nominate you: each Canadian high school can nominate only one graduating student per year. The 2027 cycle already has its dates set, with the school submitting the nominee by 27 January 2027 and you submitting the full scholarship application by 17 February 2027.
eligibility_tips: Every high school in Canada may nominate one graduating student per year, so ask early in the autumn term rather than after the winter holidays; the nomination window itself is 11-27 January 2027.

The award is aimed at STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics as a major or minor) - confirm that the programme you will enter at the partner university is in scope before you are nominated.
Student entrepreneurs are explicitly eligible, and Student Place Holders who apply after their graduating year must already be enrolled at one of the 20 partner universities.
application_tips: Prepare the three nominee documents (two letters of recommendation, an essay and a transcript) between 27 January and 17 February 2027: that three-week window is the only time you have.

Make the essay and the recommendation letters carry the three personal criteria the programme names - academic excellence, leadership, charitableness and financial need - rather than a generic achievement list.
Universities make offers between 8 March and 15 June 2027, so keep that evening window free in your own calendar and do not commit to other institutions before you have a decision.
If you missed the nomination deadline, the Student Place Holder route keeps you eligible once you are enrolled, so do not abandon the goal in your first year at a partner university.
documents: High school nomination (one per school per year)
mistakes_to_avoid: Waiting for your school to nominate you after 27 January 2027, when the nomination window has closed.
Treating the school nomination as the end of the process - your own application is due on 17 February 2027, only three weeks later.
Assuming a business or humanities degree qualifies; the scholarship targets STEM majors or minors at the 20 partner universities.
Expecting a response before 8 March 2027: university offers are only issued between 8 March and 15 June 2027.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: Registration for the 2027 cycle is open now. Diary 27 January 2027 (school nomination), 17 February 2027 (your application) and 8 March - 15 June 2027 (offers).

records.description: The University of Manitoba International Excellence Entrance Scholarship provides international students with support for their undergraduate studies, offering one award of $25,000 and two awards of $10,000 for the 2027/28 admission cycle. Awards are based on demonstrated academic achievement, leadership and community involvement. Applications open in September and all portions of the application, including the required admission application with fee, must be complete by December 1.

eligibility: International students entering an undergraduate degree programme at the University of Manitoba
$25,000 award: an average of 90 percent across five senior-level courses at the Grade 12 level
Demonstrated involvement in leadership and community activities
benefits: Support for undergraduate studies at the University of Manitoba
selection_criteria: Demonstrated academic achievement (90 percent average across five senior-level courses for the $25,000 award; minimum admission requirements for the $10,000 awards)
Demonstrated involvement in leadership and community activities
Applications of short-listed applicants are ranked 1st, 2nd and 3rd based on the award application and the admission application
official.application_process: Applications open in September and are made through the award application in addition to the admission application. All portions of the application must be complete by December 1, including the admission application and application fee, so students are encouraged to apply as early as possible. A letter of recommendation from a current teacher or principal (translated into English, if the original is not in English) is also required and is due by December 1.

deadlines.label: Complete application deadline
deadlines.note: The page states all portions of the application must be complete by December 1, including the admission application with fee; the page does not publish a separate scholarship deadline.

verification.deadline_display: December 1, 2026 (2027/28 cycle) - all portions of the application
verification.deadline_note: The page does not publish the application deadline in a date field; the deadline is stated as December 1 for all portions of the application, which is read as the 2027/28 cycle's date of 1 December 2026.
verification.application_cycle: Applications open in September for the following academic year; the 2027/28 cycle is currently open.
verification.tuition_coverage_note: Not a tuition waiver. The award is a cash prize ($25,000 or $10,000); the page does not state that tuition fees are covered.
verification.status_note: Status computed at research time (10 October 2026). The page states the 2027/28 application cycle is open, so the programme is marked OPEN.

applicant_utility.description: There is no separate scholarship competition here: the International Excellence Entrance Scholarship sits behind an admission application with a fee, and both must be complete by December 1. The award is one-time cash - $25,000 for a 90 percent average across five senior-level courses, or $10,000 if you meet the minimum admission requirements - so treat it as money toward your degree rather than a promise of free tuition.
eligibility_tips: For the $25,000 award the cut-off is an average of 90 percent across five senior-level courses at the Grade 12 level; for the $10,000 awards you need only the minimum requirements for admission, which changes how much of your effort should go into the scholarship file.
Your leadership and community involvement is a selection criterion in its own right, so document it specifically rather than as an afterthought.
application_tips: Apply as soon as applications open in September: the page encourages early application, and the deadline covers every part of the file, not just the scholarship form.
Pay the admission application fee during the application process. The scholarship application is separate from, and additional to, the admission application.
Line up your teacher or principal early: the recommendation letter must arrive by the same December 1 date, and if it is not already in English you must have it translated.

Understand the ranking mechanism: short-listed applicants are ranked 1st, 2nd and 3rd based on the award application together with the admission application, so both files must be strong and consistent.
documents: Award application (in addition to the admission application)
Letter of recommendation from a current teacher or principal (translated into English if required)
mistakes_to_avoid: Submitting only the scholarship application and forgetting the admission application and its fee, which is required for the file to be complete on 1 December.
Assuming the recommendation letter can arrive after the deadline; it is also due by December 1.
Sending an original-language recommendation letter without an English translation, which would make it unusable.
Waiting for the December deadline: ranking is based on the entire award and admission application, so early, complete files are favoured.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: Applications open in September. Everything - award application, admission application, fee and recommendation letter - must be complete by December 1 (1 December 2026 for the 2027/28 cycle).
